alan-watts.bio: Alan Watts wrote and lectured about Zen Buddhism, Taoism and their reception in the West.

ram-dass.bio:
Ram Dass (1931–2019) was an American psychologist and spiritual teacher. Born Richard Alpert, he taught at Harvard and studied psychedelics with Timothy Leary. In India in 1967, he met Neem Karoli Baba, the teacher who gave him the name Ram Dass. His 1971 book *Be Here Now* grew out of that encounter. It combined autobiography, illustrated reflections and a practical introduction to meditation and yoga.

Service became a recurring theme in his work. He helped establish the Prison-Ashram Project and the Seva Foundation, whose work includes restoring sight. After a stroke in 1997 affected his speech and mobility, he continued to teach, including at retreats on Maui. His later talks drew on the experience of depending on others for care.

[Biography from the Love Serve Remember Foundation](https://www.ramdass.org/about-ram-dass/)

bryan-johnson.bio:
Bryan Johnson founded the payments company Braintree and later Kernel, a company that develops tools for measuring brain activity. With **Blueprint**, he turned the focus of measurement on himself: he records what he eats, how he sleeps and trains, and how his test results change over time.

### Inside Blueprint

His [published protocol](https://protocol.bryanjohnson.com/) includes both a daily timetable and notes on individual experiments. Sleep is a recurring theme: Johnson describes how he tracks his resting heart rate before bed and compares it with the timing of meals and evening activities. His exercise routine combines strength, cardiovascular work, flexibility and balance.

### Reading the results

Blueprint is a record of one person's decisions and observations. A change in Johnson’s measurements cannot, on its own, tell us which intervention caused it or whether someone else would see the same result. The [archive of the original project](https://protocol-museum.bryanjohnson.com/) gives readers a way to compare earlier versions of his routine with what he publishes today.

wim-hof.bio:
Wim Hof is a Dutch endurance athlete whose public demonstrations earned him the nickname **the Iceman**. He drew attention by swimming under ice and spending long periods surrounded by ice. What began as a personal fascination became a question other people could test: how much of his response to cold could someone else learn?

### From endurance feats to teaching

Hof describes his approach as a combination of breathing exercises, exposure to cold and mental commitment. His [account of his career](https://www.wimhofmethod.com/iceman-wim-hof) traces the path from his early encounters with cold water to public challenges and the courses he developed around them.

### What researchers tested

In a [2014 controlled study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24799686/), researchers compared volunteers trained in Hof’s techniques with an untrained group during a short laboratory challenge. The trained volunteers showed a different adrenaline and inflammatory response. The experiment is interesting precisely because the subjects were ordinary volunteers. Its small size and short duration leave open what the training means for long-term health.

peter-attia.bio: Peter Attia is a physician and co-author of *Outlive*. His work covers exercise, preventive medicine and aging.

aldous-huxley.bio: Aldous Huxley wrote novels and essays, including *Brave New World* and *The Doors of Perception*.

andrew-huberman.bio: Andrew Huberman is a neuroscientist and host of *Huberman Lab*, a podcast about neuroscience and human behavior.

ben-greenfield.bio: Ben Greenfield is a fitness writer and endurance athlete who writes about training and recovery.

joseph-mercola.bio: Joseph Mercola is an osteopathic physician and author who writes about alternative medicine.

daniel-kahneman.bio: Daniel Kahneman was a psychologist whose research examined judgment and decision-making. He wrote *Thinking, Fast and Slow*.

steven-r-gundry.bio: Steven Gundry is a former cardiothoracic surgeon and author of *The Plant Paradox*.

charles-duhigg.bio: Charles Duhigg is a journalist and author of *The Power of Habit*, which explores how routines develop and change.

eric-r-braverman.bio: Eric Braverman is a physician and author who has written about brain health.

michael-greger.bio: Michael Greger is a physician and author who writes about nutrition and plant-based diets.

jason-fung.bio: Jason Fung is a nephrologist and author who writes about diabetes and fasting.
